title: The Visitors by Bryna Turner at Second Stage #thevisitors #secondstag...
transcript: The Visitors is a new family drama that's chock full of great jabs and zingers — it's a shame the plot is so predictable. When Joanna calls up her siblings for a huge favor, the fallout exposes the longstanding family dynamic that has bred resentment and eroded any sense of unconditional love. It obviously raises some questions around familial responsibility, but it's much more of a straight up drama than a problem play or think piece. Instead of sprinkling out revelations that further complicate the situation, the story is more concerned with showing us how these characters react and regress into old patterns. Although contrived and formulaic, it is a strong vehicle for realistic family dialogue and solid performances, especially from Celia Keenan-Bolger, who is desperately trying to recover from a severe case of eldest daughter syndrome. The most unbelievable part of this play is the relationship between Joanna and her partner Naomi, a woefully underwritten character who's meant to bring higher emotional stakes to the story, but ultimately is a speed bump in an otherwise taut and entertaining 90 minutes. It's still an enjoyable ride, it just presents a road well-travelled that might be easy to forget.
